mainTopic: The source that a מנחה must be מצה and guarded from חמץ, followed by the story of רבי פרידא and רבי עזרא
overview: רבי אמי quotes פסוקים showing that a מנחה should be made as מצה. רבי פרידא says he wants proof that this is לעכב, meaning the מנחה is invalid without it. רבי אמי answers from 'לא תאפה חמץ'. Then רב חסדא (שיאור), רב נחמן בר יצחק (boiled dough) and רבינא (maybe it is only a לאו) each show that the פסוק could mean something else. So the גמרא brings a ברייתא instead: the word 'תהיה' in 'מצה תהיה' makes מצה a firm requirement. רבי פרידא then asks for the source that מנחה dough must be guarded from becoming חמץ. רבי אמי reads the same word 'תהיה' as 'החייה', and the גמרא explains that the extra wording teaches both lessons. A story follows: רבי פרידא says Torah, not lineage, makes a guest worthy, and he lets in רבי עזרא. The two then trade דרשות on the words אדיר and ידיד, and the ידיד דרשה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verses showing a מנחה is eaten as מצה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי continues his answer by quoting the פסוקים about the מנחה, which end with 'it shall be eaten as מצות.'
steps.simpleTranslation: "This is the law of the מנחה: the sons of אהרן shall offer it before ה׳ in front of the altar. And what is left of it, אהרן and his sons shall eat; it shall be eaten as מצות."
steps.whatsHappening: This continues רבי אמי's answer to רבי פרידא's question about where we learn that a מנחה must be מצה. He quotes the פסוקים in ויקרא about the general law of the מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key words are 'מצות תאכל': the part of the מנחה that the כהנים eat must be מצה. This shows that the Torah wants the מנחה to be מצה. It does not yet say what happens if someone made it as חמץ anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal offering made of flour
The part that is left over after the portion burned on the altar
It shall be eaten as unleavened bread

phrases.english: "This is the law of the meal offering:
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:7–9

phrases.english: the sons of Aaron shall offer it
before ה׳, in front of the altar.
And that which is left of it
Aaron and his sons shall eat;
it shall be eaten as matzos."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אמי's answer to the question raised just before this.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'מצות תאכל' teaches that a מנחה is to be made as מצה.

steps.title: רבי פרידא sharpens his question: is it indispensable?
steps.stepSummary: רבי פרידא says the basic מצוה is obvious from those פסוקים. He is asking for a source that the requirement is לעכב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am not asking about the מצוה. What I am asking about is whether it is indispensable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פרידא tells רבי אמי that the answer missed his point. He wants a source that a מנחה not made as מצה is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many requirements in קרבנות are a מצוה to do from the start, but the offering still works if they were skipped. A requirement that is לעכב makes the offering invalid if missing. The פסוק 'מצות תאכל' proves only the first kind.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the proper way to do it from the start
Indispensable; without it, the offering is invalid
I am asking / my question is

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי פרידא doubts that a מנחה should be מצה. He accepts that fully. His question is only whether getting it wrong ruins the offering.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי פרידא speaking to רבי אמי.

phrases.english: About the מצוה I am not asking;
what I am asking about is whether it is indispensable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִצְוָה לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי, כִּי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי לְעַכֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Says the source in step 1 proves only a מצוה, not that it is לעכב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that making a מנחה as מצה is indispensable.

steps.title: Proof that it is indispensable: 'It shall not be baked as חמץ'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers that another פסוק, 'לא תאפה חמץ', adds that it must be מצה and nothing else. This shows it is לעכב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For indispensability it is also written, "It shall not be baked as חמץ"; rather, it must be מצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי gives a second פסוק to answer the sharpened question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah already said 'מצות תאכל.' Adding 'לא תאפה חמץ' repeats the idea in a negative form. That extra wording teaches that only מצה works, so a חמץ מנחה is invalid even after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall not be baked as leavened bread
Leavened dough or bread
Rather, only unleavened bread

phrases.english: He said to him: Regarding indispensability,
it is also written:
"It shall not be baked as chametz";
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:10

phrases.english: rather, it must be matzah.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעַכֵּב, נָמֵי כְּתִיב לֹא תֵאָפֶה חָמֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the sharpened question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra negative פסוק 'לא תאפה חמץ' teaches that only מצה is valid, so the requirement is לעכב.

steps.title: רב חסדא: maybe only full חמץ is excluded, not שיאור
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא challenges the reading: the פסוק forbids full חמץ, but perhaps partly leavened dough (שיאור) is still allowed. If so, the פסוק does not prove that only מצה works.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא objects: But say the verse means, "It shall not be baked as חמץ," but it may be baked as שיאור, partly leavened dough.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks רבי אמי's proof. He suggests the פסוק excludes only full חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי read 'not חמץ' as meaning 'only מצה.' רב חסדא says there may be a middle stage, שיאור, which is neither full חמץ nor real מצה. If that middle stage is acceptable, the פסוק does not show that real מצה is required.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it; challenges the statement
But perhaps say
Dough that has started to rise but is not fully חמץ

phrases.english: Rav Chisda objects to this:
But say: "It shall not be baked as chametz,"
but it may be partly leavened dough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's reading of 'לא תאפה חמץ' as 'only מצה.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Excluding חמץ does not automatically mean requiring מצה, since a middle category (שיאור) might be allowed.

steps.title: No middle category: שיאור is either מצה or חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא first tests רב חסדא's objection across the two opinions. Each opinion's שיאור counts as full מצה or full חמץ for the other תנא, so in this cross-check there is no in-between stage (step 6 shows one remains under רבי יהודה's own view).
steps.simpleTranslation: Siur according to whom? If according to רבי מאיר, then for רבי יהודה it is full matzah. If according to רבי יהודה, then for רבי מאיר it is full chametz.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which definition of שיאור רב חסדא means. It then shows that neither definition creates a real middle category.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree about what stage counts as שיאור. The earlier stage, רבי מאיר's שיאור, is still full מצה for רבי יהודה. The later stage, רבי יהודה's שיאור, is already full חמץ for רבי מאיר. So when one תנא's שיאור is judged by the other תנא, there is no middle stage. Step 6 goes on to check each תנא's own view.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom?
Fully proper matzah
Fully proper chametz

steps.whatToRemember: Judged across the two opinions, שיאור is either full מצה or full חמץ. Step 6 shows that under רבי יהודה's own view a real middle stage still exists, so רב חסדא's objection holds.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא checks an objection: it tests the objection against both sides of a מחלוקת to see where it still applies.

phrases.english: Siur according to whose definition?
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree about what counts as שיאור (פסחים 48b).

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Meir's siur,
according to Rabbi Yehuda it is full-fledged matzah;
if it is Rabbi Yehuda's siur,
according to Rabbi Meir it is full-fledged chametz.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's objection from step 4, which supports רבי אמי's proof in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב חסדא's suggestion that שיאור is a valid middle category for a מנחה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under each definition of שיאור, the other תנא treats it as full מצה or full חמץ, so no true in-between category exists.

steps.title: Checking each תנא's own שיאור: רבי מאיר's is solved, רבי יהודה's is not
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי מאיר, his own שיאור is real חמץ, since one is lashed for it. But under רבי יהודה, his own שיאור is a real in-between stage, so רב חסדא's question still stands there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you mean רבי מאיר's שיאור according to רבי מאיר himself, it is full חמץ, because he says one gets lashes for eating it. Rather, the problem is רבי יהודה's שיאור according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now checks each תנא on his own terms. For רבי מאיר there is no gap, but for רבי יהודה a gap remains, so רב חסדא's question is still alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 only showed that each תנא's שיאור counts as full מצה or full חמץ for the other תנא. Here the גמרא asks what each תנא says about his own שיאור. רבי מאיר treats his as real חמץ, since there are lashes for it, so there is no in-between. רבי יהודה's own שיאור is truly in between, so the question returns in his case.

keyTerms.meaning: Dough that has started to rise but is not fully leavened
He is lashed (punished with מלקות)
Fully leavened dough or bread

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two checks. Step 5 compared one תנא's שיאור with the other תנא's view. This step looks at each תנא's view of his own שיאור.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Meir's partly leavened dough, according to Rabbi Meir himself —
since one is lashed for it, it is full leavened bread!
Rather, the problem is Rabbi Yehuda's partly leavened dough, according to Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: For רבי יהודה, his own שיאור is truly in between, so רב חסדא's question still has room here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes further than step 5's answer by checking each תנא's own view, and finds that the gap remains under רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's proof that 'לא תאפה חמץ' means only מצה works
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי יהודה, his own שיאור is neither full חמץ nor full מצה. So the פסוק forbidding חמץ does not rule out every non-מצה dough.

steps.title: Maybe boiled dough is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק suggests that the פסוק only forbids baking the מנחה as חמץ, so boiled dough (חלוט), which is neither, might be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק objects: say that 'it shall not be baked as חמץ' means only חמץ is forbidden, but boiled dough is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: A new sage attacks רבי אמי's proof from a different direction. He points to a third kind of dough, boiled dough, that is not mentioned by the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי read 'לא תאפה חמץ' as 'only מצה.' רב נחמן בר יצחק says the פסוק may only exclude חמץ. Boiled dough is neither חמץ nor baked מצה, so the פסוק may leave it allowed, and then the proof that only מצה works would fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenges it; introduces a sage's objection
Dough scalded or boiled in hot water
But say instead; offers another possible reading

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak objects to it:
But say: "It shall not be baked as leavened bread" —
but boiled dough may be brought.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, וְאֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the שיאור challenge, a second, separate challenge is raised against רבי אמי's proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's reading of 'לא תאפה חמץ' as 'only מצה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק forbids only חמץ, so a third option like boiled dough could still be valid. That means מצה would not be לעכב.

steps.title: Boiled dough is poaching, which the Torah mentions only where it wants it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies חלוט with רביכה, poaching. Where the Torah wants poaching it says so explicitly, and here it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is boiled dough? It is poaching. If a מנחה is supposed to be poached, the Torah writes poaching about it. Here, poaching is not written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against רב נחמן בר יצחק. Boiled dough is the same as poaching, and the Torah only allows poaching where it says so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלוט is the same thing as רביכה, the poaching that the Torah mentions for a certain מנחה. Since the Torah names poaching openly where it wants it, we cannot read a hidden permission for it into 'לא תאפה חמץ'. Where poaching is not written, it is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Poaching: dough soaked or cooked in hot water and oil
What is it? Asks for a definition
It is written about it in the Torah

phrases.english: Boiled dough, what is it? It is poaching.

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּאִיכָּא רְבוּכָה – כְּתִיב בָּהּ רְבוּכָה,
phrases.english: If it is an offering that is poached, poaching is written about it,
and here poaching is not written about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן בר יצחק's suggestion that boiled dough is allowed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that 'לא תאפה חמץ' leaves room for boiled dough in a regular מנחה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Boiled dough is poaching, which the Torah mentions openly only where it wants it. So it cannot be assumed where it is not written.

steps.title: Maybe poaching is required in one place and optional elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe where poaching is written it is the required מצוה, but elsewhere the person may choose poaching or מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: where poaching is written, the מצוה is to poach. Where it is not written, he may bring it poached if he wants, or as מצה if he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer from step 8. The fact that the Torah wrote poaching in one place may only show where poaching is required, not where it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 claimed that 'poaching is not written here' means it is not allowed. This step offers another reading: writing poaching may only make it the preferred מצוה in that case. Elsewhere it could still be one choice next to מצה, and then רבי אמי's proof that only מצה works is not conclusive.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the preferred way to do it, not an absolute requirement
If he wants; the person may choose
Let him bring

steps.confusionAlert: Here מצוה means the proper way to do it at the start, not that anything else is פסול. That gap is exactly the point of the challenge.

phrases.english: But say: an offering about which poaching is written —
the מצוה is to bring it poached,
and one about which poaching is not written —
if he wants, let him bring it poached,
if he wants, let him bring it as matza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 8 and brings רב נחמן בר יצחק's question back to life.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 8's reasoning that poaching is allowed only where it is written
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Writing poaching in one place may only make it required there, without forbidding it elsewhere. So boiled dough could be an option, and מצה would not be לעכב.

steps.title: Maybe the פסוק is only a לאו, not a reason to make the מנחה פסול
steps.stepSummary: רבינא suggests that 'לא תאפה חמץ' may only make the person guilty of a לאו, while the מנחה itself stays valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objects: say that 'it shall not be baked as חמץ' only puts the man under a simple prohibition, but the offering is not made פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: A third sage attacks רבי אמי's proof. He says the פסוק may only be a prohibition on the person, not a rule about whether the מנחה is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי needed the פסוק to show that a non-מצה מנחה is פסול (לעכב). רבינא points out that a לאו can punish the person without making the offering invalid. If so, the פסוק proves nothing about לעכב.

keyTerms.meaning: Just a prohibition, with no further effect
To become invalid (פסול)
To make the person stand under (a prohibition)

steps.whyThisMatters: It separates two ideas: a sin by the person and a פסול in the offering. A prohibition does not automatically make the offering invalid.

phrases.english: Ravina objects to it: But say:
"It shall not be baked as leavened bread" —
serves to place the man under a mere prohibition,
but the offering itself is not invalidated?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, separate challenge to רבי אמי's proof. It no longer argues about kinds of dough, but about what the פסוק does.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's claim that 'לא תאפה חמץ' shows מצה is לעכב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק that forbids something can make the person guilty without making the offering פסול. So the פסוק does not prove that the requirement is לעכב.

steps.title: So where do we learn that a מנחה must be מצה?
steps.stepSummary: After the challenges to רבי אמי's proof, the גמרא asks for a new source that a מנחה not made as מצה is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, from where do we learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier proof from 'לא תאפה חמץ' was knocked down, so the גמרא asks again for a source. It is setting up the next step, where a ברייתא gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 4 to 10 showed that 'לא תאפה חמץ' could mean something else: perhaps שיאור is allowed (רב חסדא), perhaps boiled dough is allowed (רב נחמן בר יצחק), or perhaps it is only a לאו with the מנחה still valid (רבינא). So the גמרא still needs a source that being מצה is required for the מנחה to be valid at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, but instead. It signals dropping the earlier idea.
From where do we know this? A request for a source.

phrases.english: Rather, from where do we derive it?
phrases.notes: Where do we learn that a מנחה that is not מצה doesn't count, now that the earlier proof fell apart?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the series of challenges by abandoning רבי אמי's derivation and seeking a new one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that being מצה is required for a מנחה to be valid.

steps.title: A ברייתא learns it from the word 'תהיה'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the word 'תהיה' in 'מצה תהיה' turns מצה from a preferred מצוה into an absolute requirement.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'מצה'. You might think it is only a מצוה, the right way to do it. So the פסוק says 'תהיה', 'it shall be', which shows the Torah made it a firm requirement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. The extra word 'תהיה' shows that a מנחה must be מצה, or it is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'תהיה', we would think being מצה is only the ideal way to make the מנחה, and that it is still valid after the fact if made differently. The word 'תהיה', 'it shall be', shows the Torah sets it as a fixed requirement. This answers רבינא's point from step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought. It introduces a possibility the ברייתא will reject.
Here: the ideal way to do it, but not something that holds it back from being valid.
The פסוק teaches us. It introduces the word that settles the question.
Set it as an obligation. It is required, and without it the מנחה is invalid.

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'תהיה' in 'מצה תהיה' makes מצה a must for a מנחה. If it is not מצה, the מנחה is invalid.

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'Matza.' One might think it is only a מצוה?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:5

phrases.english: The verse states: 'It shall be'
The verse established it as an obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'תהיה' in 'מצה תהיה' makes מצה an absolute requirement for a מנחה.

steps.title: רבי פרידא asks about kneading and guarding the dough
steps.stepSummary: רבי פרידא asks רבי אמי for the source that מנחות are kneaded with lukewarm water and guarded from becoming חמץ. He suggests learning it from פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פרידא asked רבי אמי: From where do we learn that all the מנחות are kneaded with lukewarm water, and that one must guard them so they do not become חמץ? Should we learn it from פסח, where it is written 'and you shall guard the מצות'?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבי פרידא wants a source for guarding מנחה dough from becoming חמץ, and he offers פסח as a possible source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know a מנחה must be מצה. This question is about the process: the dough must be actively watched while it is made. The פסוק about פסח, 'ושמרתם את המצות', commands guarding מצה, so he asks whether מנחות borrow that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Are kneaded.
Lukewarm water.
One guards them, watching the dough so it does not become חמץ.
Become חמץ, leavened.
Shall we learn it from another source?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינַּהּ רַבִּי פְּרִידָא מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Perida asked of Rabbi Ami:
From where is it derived for all the meal offerings
that they are kneaded with lukewarm water,
and one guards them so that they do not become leavened?
Shall we learn it from Passover,
as it is written: 'And you shall guard the matzot.'
phrases.notes: שמות 12:17

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינַּהּ רַבִּי פְּרִידָא מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about how מנחה dough is prepared.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for kneading מנחות with lukewarm water and guarding them from becoming חמץ, possibly learned from פסח.

steps.title: רבי אמי: the מנחה's own פסוק teaches guarding
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers that we do not need פסח. The מנחה's own פסוק says 'מצה תהיה', which hints at 'החייה', keep it alive as מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: In the מנחה itself it is written 'מצה תהיה', 'it shall be מצה'. Read it as 'החייה', keep it as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers that the guarding rule comes straight from the מנחה's own פסוק, not from פסח. He reads 'תהיה' as a hint to 'החייה', preserve it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תהיה' and 'החייה' sound alike. רבי אמי reads 'it shall be מצה' as 'keep it in its מצה state', which means guarding the dough so it does not become חמץ. A source in the topic itself is better than borrowing from פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: In the topic itself, here the פסוק about the מנחה.
Keep it alive. Preserve it in its מצה state, a play on the word 'תהיה'.

phrases.english: He said to him:
In it itself it is written: 'It shall be matza,'
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק about the מנחה itself, ויקרא 2:5, so there is no need to borrow from פסח.

phrases.english: Keep it alive.
phrases.notes: A play on sounds: 'תהיה' is read like 'החייה', keep the מצה as it is so it doesn't turn חמץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי פרידא's question and turns down the source from פסח.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'תהיה' in 'מצה תהיה', read as 'החייה', teaches that the dough must be guarded.

steps.title: But 'תהיה' was already used for something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 'תהיה' was already used in step 12 to show that מצה is a must for a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you already take that word to teach that it is required?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אמי. The same word 'תהיה' was already used in the ברייתא for a different lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual idea is that one word teaches one lesson. Step 12 used 'תהיה' to show that being מצה is required for the מנחה to be valid. So how can the same word also teach guarding the dough?

keyTerms.meaning: You already took it out and used it for another lesson.
To hold back. A requirement without which the offering is invalid.

phrases.english: But didn't you already use it to teach that it is indispensable?
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא in step 12, which used 'תהיה' to make מצה a must.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the derivation in step 14 by pointing to step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's use of 'תהיה' to teach guarding the dough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word was already used to show that מצה is required, so it cannot also teach a second lesson.

steps.title: 'תהיה' is extra, so it teaches two things
steps.stepSummary: The Torah could have written 'מצה היא'. Writing 'תהיה' instead gives room to learn both lessons.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it taught only one thing, the פסוק should have written 'it is מצה'. Why write 'it shall be'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Because the Torah chose the longer wording 'תהיה' instead of the simple 'היא', the word carries two lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain way to say it would be 'מצה היא'. The unusual choice of 'תהיה' signals extra meaning. So it teaches both that מצה is required and that the dough must be guarded.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. If the word taught only one thing.
Let the פסוק write instead. Showing another wording the Torah could have used.
Learn two things from it.

steps.whatToRemember: 'מצה תהיה' teaches two lessons: a מנחה must be מצה or it is invalid, and the dough must be guarded so it does not become חמץ.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write: 'It is matza,'
Why does it say 'It shall be'?
Learn from it two things.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן לִיכְתּוֹב קְרָא מַצָּה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the פסוק allows two lessons.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'תהיה' can teach only one lesson, so it cannot teach guarding the dough.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since 'מצה היא' would have been enough, the word 'תהיה' teaches both that מצה is required and that the dough must be guarded.

steps.title: The רבנן announce that רבי עזרא is waiting at the door
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן tell רבי פרידא that רבי עזרא, who has a famous family tree going back to עזרא, is standing at the gate.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רבי פרידא: רבי עזרא, the grandson of רבי אבטולס, who is ten generations after רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who is ten generations after עזרא, is standing at the gate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about רבי פרידא, the sage from the previous steps. This line sets up the story: a guest with very important ancestors is waiting outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן don't just say a guest is outside. They list his whole family tree, as if his lineage were the reason to let him in. That detail sets up רבי פרידא's reaction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: His son's son, a grandson
Tenth, here meaning ten generations down
Is standing at the gate or door

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rabbi Perida:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֶזְרָא בַּר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַבְטוֹלָס,
phrases.english: Rabbi Ezra, the grandson of Rabbi Avtolus,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהוּא עֲשִׂירִי לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה,
phrases.english: who is the tenth generation from Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
who is the tenth generation from Ezra,
is standing at the gate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the halachic discussion and opens a story about רבי פרידא, who appeared in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A guest of very great lineage is waiting at רבי פרידא's door.

steps.title: רבי פרידא asks why lineage matters and says Torah is what counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי פרידא asks what the long family tree is for. A Torah scholar is worthy whether or not he has lineage, but someone with lineage and no Torah is worth nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: What is all this? If he is a man of Torah, he is worthy. If he is a man of Torah and a man of lineage, he is worthy. But if he is a man of lineage and not a man of Torah, let fire consume him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פרידא pushes back on the long introduction. He wants to know one thing only: is this guest a Torah scholar?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי פרידא lays out three cases. Torah alone makes a person worthy, and Torah with lineage also makes him worthy, so lineage adds nothing needed. Lineage without Torah earns the harshest words, 'let fire consume him.' So his real question is whether the guest learns Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: What is all this? Why so much detail?
A man of Torah, a Torah scholar
A man of ancestors, someone from a distinguished family
Is fitting, is worthy
Let fire consume him, a very strong rejection

steps.confusionAlert: רבי פרידא is not against lineage. Case two, Torah plus lineage, is also 'worthy.' His point is that lineage cannot replace Torah.
steps.whyThisMatters: It is a clear statement of values: a person's worth comes from his own Torah, not from his ancestors.

phrases.english: He said: What is all this?
If he is a man of Torah, he is worthy;

phrases.aramaic: אִי בַּר אוֹרְיָין וּבַר אֲבָהָן – יָאֵי,
phrases.english: if he is a man of Torah and a man of lineage, he is worthy;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי בַּר אֲבָהָן וְלָא בַּר אוֹרְיָין –
phrases.english: but if he is a man of lineage and not a man of Torah,
let fire consume him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the lineage-heavy announcement in step 17 by asking about the guest's Torah instead.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי עזרא is a Torah scholar, which is the only thing that decides whether he deserves to come in.

steps.title: He is a Torah scholar, so let him come in
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that רבי עזרא is a Torah scholar, and רבי פרידא tells them to let him in.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: He is a man of Torah. He said to them: Let him enter and come.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן answer רבי פרידא's question, and he agrees to let the guest in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רבי עזרא is shown to be a בר אוריין, he fits the 'worthy' cases from step 18. The door opens because of his Torah, not because of his family tree.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him enter and come

phrases.english: They said to him: He is a man of Torah.
He said to them: Let him enter and come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עזרא is a Torah scholar, so he may come in.

steps.title: רבי פרידא opens a דרשה: Israel asks ה׳ for credit
steps.stepSummary: Seeing that רבי עזרא is upset, רבי פרידא expounds a פסוק in תהלים. In his reading, כנסת ישראל asks ה׳ to give her credit for making Him known in the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw that his mind was troubled. He began and said: 'You said to ה׳, You are my Lord; my good is not upon You.' כנסת ישראל said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the world, give me credit for making You known in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פרידא sees that his guest is troubled, so he begins a דרשה on a פסוק. This step gives the first half of the דרשה: כנסת ישראל's request.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'You are my Lord' are read as כנסת ישראל saying she declared ה׳'s name in the world. She asks ה׳ to credit her for it. The second half of the same פסוק will be read as ה׳'s reply in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind was troubled or upset
He opened, began a דרשה
The Congregation of Israel, the Jewish people as a whole
Give me credit, acknowledge the good I did

phrases.english: He saw him, that his mind was troubled,
phrases.notes: רבי פרידא is the one looking, and רבי עזרא, who just came in, is the one who is upset.

phrases.english: he began and said:
"You said to the Lord: You are my Lord;
my good is not upon You,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 16:2

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: The Congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:

phrases.aramaic: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, הַחֲזֵק לִי טוֹבָה
phrases.english: Master of the world, give me credit
for I made You known in the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַזְיֵיהּ דַּהֲוָה עֲכִירָא דַּעְתֵּיהּ, פְּתַח וַאֲמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After letting רבי עזרא in, רבי פרידא responds to his troubled mood with a דרשה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the first half of the פסוק, כנסת ישראל asks ה׳ to credit her for making His name known.

steps.title: ה׳ answers that the credit belongs to the אבות
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ replies with the end of the same פסוק: He gives credit only to אברהם, יצחק, and יעקב, who made Him known first. The next פסוק is brought as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: 'My good is not upon you.' I credit no one except אברהם, יצחק, and יעקב, who first made Me known in the world, as it says: 'For the holy ones who are in the land, and the mighty ones, all My desire is in them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The דרשה finishes: ה׳ answers כנסת ישראל's request. The words 'טובתי בל עליך' are read as ה׳ saying, 'I don't owe you credit.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The credit goes to the ones who started it, the אבות, who made ה׳ known first. The proof is the next פסוק, which calls 'the holy ones in the land' the ones ה׳ delights in. The דרשה stresses the special greatness of the first ancestors, which seems to be a gentle way of honoring רבי עזרא's family after the strong words in step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not give credit
First, at the very beginning
The mighty or great ones

steps.whatToRemember: In this story Torah learning is what makes a person worthy, yet the דרשה also shows that ה׳ values the ancestors who first made His name known.

phrases.english: He said to her: "My good is not upon you":
phrases.notes: The same words from the פסוק are now read as ה׳'s answer: 'Your good deed doesn't earn you the credit.'

phrases.english: I give credit only
to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
who first made Me known in the world,
as it is stated: "For the holy ones who are in the land,
and the mighty ones, in whom is all My delight."
phrases.notes: תהלים 16:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives ה׳'s reply to the request in step 20, using the second half of the same פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The credit goes only to the אבות, who first made ה׳ known, as shown by תהלים 16:3.

steps.title: רבי עזרא opens a word-play on 'אדיר'
steps.stepSummary: Hearing רבי פרידא say the word אדיר, רבי עזרא opens with a riddle-like sentence that uses אדיר four times.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי עזרא heard רבי פרידא say 'אדיר', he began and said: Let the Mighty One come and exact payment for the mighty ones, from the mighty ones, through the mighty ones.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עזרא picks up the word אדיר from רבי פרידא's דרשה and builds a short, puzzling sentence around it. This step sets up the next one, where each אדיר will be explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עזרא shows that he is a real תלמיד חכם by matching רבי פרידא's דרשה with one of his own. On purpose, the sentence is unclear until we know who each 'mighty one' refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: Mighty, powerful, or excellent
He opened and said, meaning he began a דרשה
He will exact payment or punishment

phrases.english: When he heard him say "addir" (mighty),
he began and said:
Let the Mighty One come
and exact payment for the mighty ones
from the mighty ones, through the mighty ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּשַׁמְעֵיהּ דְּקָאָמַר אַדִּיר, פָּתַח וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עזרא responds to רבי פרידא's דרשה by building on its key word, אדיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A riddle-sentence: the Mighty One will punish the mighty on behalf of the mighty through the mighty.

steps.title: Explaining each 'אדיר' with a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: Each אדיר is identified, with a פסוק for each: ה׳‎, ישראל, the מצרים, and the waters of the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The Mighty One' is ה׳, as it says 'Mighty on high is ה׳.' 'For the mighty ones' means ישראל, as it says 'and the mighty, in whom is all My delight.' 'From the mighty ones' means the מצרים, as it says 'they sank like lead in the mighty waters.' 'Through the mighty ones' means the waters, as it says 'above the sounds of many waters, the mighty breakers of the sea.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עזרא solves his own riddle. He shows who each 'mighty one' is and proves each one from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once it is decoded, the sentence describes קריעת ים סוף‎. ה׳ punished the מצרים for what they did to ישראל, and He did it by drowning them in the sea. Every word is tied to a פסוק that uses the same word אדיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He: ה׳
They sank like lead (from שירת הים)
Breakers (crashing waves) of the sea

steps.whatToRemember: The four אדירים are ה׳‎, ישראל, the מצרים, and the sea. Together they describe ה׳ punishing מצרים at the sea for ישראל's sake.

phrases.aramaic: יָבֹא אַדִּיר – זֶה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: "Let the Mighty One come": this is the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it is written: "Mighty on high is ה׳."
phrases.notes: תהלים 93:4

phrases.english: "And exact payment for the mighty ones": these are ישראל,
as it is said: "And the mighty, in whom is all My delight."
phrases.notes: תהלים 16:3. This is the same פסוק רבי פרידא just used.

phrases.english: "From the mighty ones": these are the Egyptians,
as it is written: "The mighty sank like lead in the waters."
phrases.notes: שמות 15:10

phrases.english: "Through the mighty ones": these are the waters,
as it is said: "Above the sounds of many waters,
the mighty breakers of the sea."
phrases.notes: תהלים 93:4

steps.triggerLanguage: יָבֹא אַדִּיר – זֶה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decodes the riddle-sentence from step 22 phrase by phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ punished the מצרים for ישראל's sake by drowning them in the sea.

steps.title: A second word-play on 'ידיד'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עזרא gives another riddle-sentence, this time using ידיד (beloved one) six times.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the beloved one, son of a beloved one, come and build the beloved thing for the Beloved One, in the portion of the beloved one, and let the beloved ones gain atonement through it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עזרא offers a second puzzle-sentence in the same style, now built on the word ידיד. This sets up the explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as before, the sentence is unclear until each ידיד is identified. The words 'build' and 'gain atonement' already hint that the sentence is about building the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Beloved one, dear friend
In his portion (of land)
They will gain atonement

phrases.english: Let the beloved one, son of a beloved one, come,
and build the beloved thing for the Beloved One
in the portion of the beloved one,
and let the beloved ones gain atonement through it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel word-play sentence following the אדיר one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A riddle-sentence about a beloved one building something beloved for the Beloved One, through which beloved ones gain atonement.

steps.title: The first 'ידיד' is שלמה המלך
steps.stepSummary: The first ידיד is identified as שלמה המלך, who was given the name ידידיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Let the beloved one come': this is שלמה המלך, as it is written: 'And He sent by the hand of נתן the prophet, and he called his name ידידיה, for ה׳'s sake.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עזרא begins decoding the ידיד sentence, starting with the first word. The rest of the explanation continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמה is called ידיד because ה׳ gave him the name ידידיה through נתן הנביא. That fits the sentence, since שלמה is the one who built the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Beloved of ה׳, a name given to שלמה
For ה׳'s sake

phrases.english: "Let the beloved one come": this is King Solomon,
as it is written: "And He sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet,
and he called his name Yedidya, for ה׳'s sake."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 12:25

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins decoding the ידיד sentence from step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first ידיד is שלמה המלך, called ידידיה by ה׳.
